item_arguments.argument: Choose compact sets with probabilities tending to one, take the closed rational span of their countable dense union, and use Hahn–Banach to extend continuous linear functionals from E to the ambient Banach space.

Write g=w−w0 and c=log E0 e^g. Bound |c|≤r, apply the exponential Taylor remainder to the centered g for directional KL, and bound the normalized log-density ratio pointwise for Hellinger and its second moment.
Use the mean-value bound for Ψ, differentiate the Bernoulli directional KL in its second logit, and bound both Bernoulli log-probability derivatives by R.

Compute the normal KL formula and expand the log likelihood ratio as a constant plus linear and centered quadratic functions of the true Gaussian error; bound the scale-only term by its vanishing first derivative at σ0.

Complete the square to compute the scalar Gaussian moment generating function and the noncentral squared-normal moment generating function; bound the latter near zero and optimize the exponential-Markov inequality.

Bound the integrated likelihood ratio in expectation using independence and Tonelli; Jensen lower-bounds the denominator by the prior-averaged log likelihood, whose mean and variance are bounded by nε², and Chebyshev gives the stated event.
Split the likelihood numerator into tested sieve mass and sieve tail, change measure to bound their expectations, and apply Markov after dividing by the denominator lower bound.

Cover the mean functions; use Gaussian linear-score tests when the empirical mean distance is large and upper/lower residual-energy tests when the scale distance is large; union-bound the finite cover and use the Gaussian quadratic tail bound.
The norm ball {‖W‖<ε} is contained in {|ℓ(W)|<‖ℓ‖ε}; bound the latter by the maximum density of its nondegenerate scalar Gaussian law and use the nonnegative RKHS cost.

Use the exact half-squared RKHS concentration convention and its support/sieve interfaces; prove model-specific likelihood-distance bounds; apply IID entropy tests and denominator bounds in the first two branches, and direct Gaussian score/energy tests with a non-IID denominator in fixed design. The fixed-scale local-mass gap remains escalated.
Verification: compute the L² norm, normalizer and Hellinger affinity explicitly; the normalized prior density concentrates on the shrinking spike.
Verification: the prior is a point mass on the zero function, so its RKHS approximation and centered small-ball costs vanish; calculate the interval mass and compare log n with log log n.
Verification: compute the normalizer, RKHS approximation term and scalar Gaussian small-ball lower bound; then normalize the identical likelihoods.
Verification: evaluate the link constants, concentration function and L²(G) identification, then instantiate the binary-regression branch.
Verification: compute the scalar GP concentration bound, the uniform scale interval mass, and verify the fixed design and compact scale hypotheses.
